questions.prompt: You assign the built-in Allowed locations policy, effect deny, to a subscription that already contains VMs in a region not on the list. What happens to those VMs?
options: They are deleted within 24 hours
They are moved to an allowed region
They keep running and are reported as non-compliant; new or updated deployments that break the rule are denied
They are stopped until an administrator approves them
questions.explanation: For deny, existing resources that match the rule are marked non-compliant. New and updated resources are denied at request time.
why_not: A deny policy never deletes or changes existing resources.
Policy doesn't move resources; moving doesn't change a resource's region anyway.
No policy effect stops or deallocates resources.
questions.clue: "already contains VMs": deny policies block new requests; existing resources are only reported non-compliant.

questions.prompt: Every existing and future resource in a resource group must carry the resource group's CostCenter tag. What should you use?
options: The Inherit a tag from the resource group policy (modify) with a remediation task, using the assignment's managed identity
A CanNotDelete lock on the resource group
Nothing: resources inherit resource group tags automatically
The Require a tag on resources policy (deny)
questions.explanation: modify adds the tag to new and updated resources at request time. A remediation task, running as the assignment's managed identity, fixes existing resources.
why_not: Locks prevent change or deletion; they don't add tags.
Tags aren't inherited.
deny blocks new non-compliant resources but never adds the tag, and does nothing to existing ones.
questions.clue: "every existing and future resource" gets the tag: a modify policy for new ones, plus remediation for existing ones.

questions.prompt: One resource group must be left out of a subscription-wide policy for six months, and auditors must still see that it is out of compliance by agreement. What should you configure?
options: An exclusion (notScopes) on the assignment
Enforcement mode DoNotEnforce on the assignment
A ReadOnly lock on the resource group
A policy exemption with the Waiver category and an expiry date
questions.explanation: Exempted resources remain visible as Exempted in compliance reports. Waiver records accepted non-compliance, and expiresOn ends the exemption automatically.
why_not: Excluded resources aren't evaluated or counted, so auditors wouldn't see them at all.
That would stop enforcement for the whole subscription, not one resource group.
A lock doesn't change policy evaluation.
questions.clue: "left out" but "auditors must still see": an exemption (Waiver) with an expiry, not an exclusion.

questions.prompt: A resource group contains a storage account with a CanNotDelete lock. The resource group itself has no lock. A subscription Owner tries to delete the resource group. What happens?
options: Everything except the storage account is deleted
The whole delete fails; nothing in the resource group is deleted
The delete succeeds because Owner overrides locks
The storage account is moved to a new resource group
questions.explanation: A Delete lock on any resource in the group blocks the entire resource group delete. Remove the lock first.
why_not: Resource group deletion is all or nothing; a partial delete isn't possible.
Locks apply to every user and role, Owner included.
Azure never moves resources to work around a lock.
questions.clue: "CanNotDelete lock" on a resource inside the group: the whole resource group delete fails.

questions.prompt: After an administrator adds a ReadOnly lock to a resource group, users report they can no longer restart a VM in it and an app can't retrieve the storage account keys. Why?
options: ReadOnly blocks POST operations, and restarting a VM and listing storage account keys are POST requests
ReadOnly also locks the data plane
The lock removed the users' role assignments
ReadOnly locks deallocate VMs
questions.explanation: Microsoft documents that ReadOnly locks block POST requests, including listing storage account keys and starting or restarting VMs.
why_not: Locks apply to the control plane only; the issue is POST operations on the control plane.
Locks don't change role assignments.
Locks don't change the state of resources.
questions.clue: "can no longer restart a VM" and "retrieve keys": ReadOnly also blocks POST actions.

questions.prompt: You must prevent the accidental deletion of resources in three subscriptions that share a management group. Where can you apply a resource lock?
options: On the management group, so all three subscriptions inherit it
On the root management group
On the Microsoft Entra tenant
On each subscription (or lower); locks can't be applied to management groups
questions.explanation: Locks can be set on subscriptions, resource groups and resources, and they inherit downwards. Management groups can't be locked.
why_not: You can't add a lock to a management group.
The root is a management group; locks can't be applied there either.
Locks are Azure Resource Manager objects on subscriptions, resource groups and resources.
questions.clue: "share a management group" tempts you, but locks go on subscriptions, resource groups or resources.

questions.sub_skill: Apply and manage tags on resources
questions.prompt: Resource group RG1 has the tag Department = Finance. A VM created in RG1 afterwards has no tags. What explains this?
options: Tags take 24 hours to propagate to child resources
Resources don't inherit tags from their resource group
VMs don't support tags
The tag name is case-sensitive and didn't match
questions.explanation: Tags apply only to the object you set them on. Use an inherit-tag policy (modify) to copy them to resources.
why_not: There's no propagation; tags are never inherited.
Virtual machines support tags.
Tag names are case-insensitive, and nothing was copied to compare anyway.
questions.clue: "has the tag" on the resource group, "no tags" on the VM: tags don't inherit.

questions.sub_skill: Apply and manage tags on resources
questions.prompt: A finance analyst must be able to add and change tags on any resource in a subscription, but must not be able to change the resources themselves. Which role should you assign?
options: Contributor
Reader
Tag Contributor
Resource Policy Contributor
questions.explanation: Tag Contributor grants write access to the tags resource type, so it can tag resources without access to the resources themselves. Microsoft notes one catch: it can't apply tags to resources or resource groups through the Azure portal, only through Azure PowerShell or the REST API (it can tag subscriptions in the portal).
why_not: Contributor can change the resources themselves.
Reader can't write tags.
That role manages policies, not tags on resources.
questions.clue: "add and change tags" but "not change the resources": Tag Contributor.

questions.prompt: You must move a virtual network and its dependent resources to a subscription that belongs to a different Microsoft Entra tenant. What is correct?
options: A resource move doesn't support moving to another tenant; associate the subscription with that tenant or re-create the resources
Use Move-AzResource with -DestinationSubscriptionId
Move the resource group to the other subscription
Export the resources as a template and use Move-AzResource on the template
questions.explanation: Moves are supported within one tenant only. Otherwise, change the subscription's directory or re-create the resources.
why_not: Cross-subscription moves require both subscriptions to be in the same tenant.
You can't move a resource group to another subscription at all.
Templates aren't moved; a template can only re-create resources.
questions.clue: "different Microsoft Entra tenant": a resource move can't cross tenants.

questions.prompt: You start moving a VM and its dependent resources from RG1 to RG2 in the same subscription. During the move, what is true?
options: The VM is deallocated until the move finishes
The VM's region changes to RG2's region
RG1 and RG2 are locked for changes, up to four hours; the VM keeps running; its resource ID will change
Only RG1 is locked; you can still create resources in RG2
questions.explanation: Both resource groups are locked for create, delete and update for up to four hours. Resources keep running, and the resource ID changes to reflect the new group.
why_not: Resources keep operating normally during a move.
A move changes only the resource group or subscription, never the region.
Both source and target resource groups are locked.
questions.clue: "during the move": both resource groups are locked for changes; the resources keep running.

questions.prompt: After an acquisition, you use Change directory to associate a subscription with your tenant. Users report they can no longer manage its resources. Why?
options: Role assignments take 24 hours to replicate to the new tenant
Changing directory permanently deletes all Azure role assignments and custom roles for the subscription
Users must re-register the resource providers
Change directory moved the resources to a new region
questions.explanation: Role assignments and custom roles are permanently deleted when a subscription moves to another directory. Re-create them in the target tenant.
why_not: They aren't replicated at all; they're deleted.
Resource provider registration isn't what removed their access.
Changing directory doesn't move resources.
questions.clue: "Change directory": role assignments in the subscription are deleted and must be re-created.

questions.prompt: You move a subscription from management group MG-Sandbox to MG-Production. What happens to the policies and role assignments applied at MG-Production?
options: Nothing, until you re-assign each policy to the subscription
The subscription keeps MG-Sandbox's assignments and adds MG-Production's
The move is blocked until MG-Production's policies are exempted
The subscription now inherits them, and no longer inherits those from MG-Sandbox
questions.explanation: A subscription that moves to a management group inherits all user access and policies from its new parent chain.
why_not: Inheritance is automatic; a subscription inherits from its parent management group.
A subscription has one parent and inherits only from its current chain.
Moves aren't blocked by the new parent's policies in this way.
questions.clue: "move a subscription" between management groups: it inherits from its new parent only.

questions.sub_skill: Manage costs by using alerts, budgets, and Azure Advisor recommendations
questions.prompt: A monthly budget with an Actual 100% threshold fires, but the VMs keep running and costs keep rising. What should you add so that crossing the budget deallocates lab VMs?
options: An action group on the budget notification that runs automation, such as a runbook that deallocates VMs
Set the budget's reset period to daily
Change the threshold type to Forecasted
Enable the spending cap on the budget
questions.explanation: A budget only notifies. An action group attached to the notification can trigger automation that acts.
why_not: Budgets never stop resources, whatever their reset period.
A forecasted alert only warns earlier; it doesn't act.
Budgets have no spending cap; they notify.
questions.clue: "VMs keep running": a budget only notifies; an action group running automation is what acts.

questions.sub_skill: Manage costs by using alerts, budgets, and Azure Advisor recommendations
questions.prompt: Advisor keeps recommending you shut down a VM that is busy only during month-end payroll processing. What should you change?
options: The VM's size, to a larger one
Advisor's lookback period for VM right-sizing, for example to 30 days
The subscription's budget threshold
Nothing; Advisor recommendations can't be configured
questions.explanation: The default lookback is seven days. You can set 14, 21, 30, 60 or 90 days so that monthly peaks are included.
why_not: That would increase cost and doesn't address how Advisor evaluates the VM.
Budgets don't influence Advisor recommendations.
Advisor lets you configure the right-sizing lookback period and CPU filter.
questions.clue: "busy only during month-end": a 7-day lookback misses it; lengthen Advisor's lookback.

questions.prompt: New subscriptions created by developers should automatically fall under the management group where your sandbox policies are assigned, not under the root. What should you configure?
options: A policy at the root management group that moves subscriptions
A ReadOnly lock on the root management group
The default management group for new subscriptions in the hierarchy settings
Nothing: new subscriptions inherit the creator's management group
questions.explanation: New subscriptions default to the root management group unless you set a different default management group in the hierarchy settings.
why_not: Policy doesn't move subscriptions between management groups.
Management groups can't be locked.
New subscriptions land under the root management group by default.
questions.clue: "new subscriptions automatically" under a management group: set the default management group.

questions.prompt: You're designing a management group hierarchy that mirrors your organisation: Root > Company > Region > Country > Division > Department > Team > Project, with subscriptions under Project. Will Azure accept it?
options: Yes; management groups have no depth limit
Yes, as long as there are fewer than 10,000 management groups
Only if each level contains a single subscription
No; a management group tree supports up to six levels of depth, not counting the root or the subscription level
questions.explanation: Below the root, Company through Project is seven levels, one more than the six-level maximum. 10,000 is the separate limit on the number of management groups per directory.
why_not: There is a documented limit of six levels of depth.
10,000 is the count limit; depth is limited separately to six levels.
The number of subscriptions per level has nothing to do with the depth limit.
questions.clue: "Root > ... > Project" with seven levels below the root: the limit is six levels of depth.
